title: Hof apply operation event
description: One record of the append-only log a running `hofctl apply` both streams to stdout (bounded NDJSON - one line per event, no other output interleaved on stdout) and durably appends to the target's own operation journal (see operation-journal-v1.schema.json) - the exact same shape for both, so `hofctl apply`'s own live progress output is never a lossy or reformatted view of what's actually durable. `step` is one plan-v2 operation's own `id` (e.g. "003.service.start.gateway") - never a free-form message. Resumability: for a given step, its most recent event (by attempt, then phase) decides what a later `apply --resume` does - `succeeded` skips it; `failed` is fatal unless the operator starts a fresh bootstrap; a `started` with no later `succeeded`/`failed` for the same step+attempt is an unknown outcome and blocks resume entirely, never guessed at.

operationId.description: The whole apply run this event belongs to - matches the run's own operation-journal-v1 and operation-lock-v1 operationId.

step.description: The bound plan-v2's own operation id this event is about - see plan-v1/v2's operationId pattern.

attempt.description: 1 for a step's first try; a resumed step that previously failed and is being retried increments this, never reuses attempt 1's own record.

phase.description: started: about to run this step, before any target-side effect. succeeded: the step's own target-side effect completed and was confirmed. failed: the step did not complete - `error` is always present and sanitized.

error.description: Only for phase: failed - a short, sanitized diagnostic. Never a raw exception dump, a secret value, decrypted content, an environment variable's value, or an SSH private-key path.
